name: Liinks
description: Link-in-bio / multi-link landing pages for creators and brand teams — customize, auto-pull Instagram links, track clicks. Starter ~$5/mo, Pro ~$12/mo. US, founded 2020.

mentions.evidence: ~$31.2k MRR, 5,419 active subscriptions, ~$32.7k L30, ~$1.76M all-time, ~10,000 users claimed, founded May 2020, US. Last sync Oct 2, 2026.
mentions.indieAngle: Own a thin, high-volume creator utility (link page, media kit, tipping page) with cheap seats and brutal retention via habit.

whyItPrints: Linktree-shaped infra with real Stripe scale: thousands of paying subs and $1.7M+ all-time. Unsexy "one URL for everything" plumbing that creators renew without thinking.
whyThisMatters:
Creators and small businesses use Liinks as the one link in a bio. Links, photos, videos, forms, FAQs, testimonials, and the latest Instagram posts can sit on that page, grouped into tabs and folders. It can work as a small site rather than a bare list of URLs. You get click stats, a QR code, and your own address on the liinks domain.

There's a 14-day trial, and you can cancel. The starter plan covers unlimited blocks, social accounts, themes, analytics, and that custom URL. The higher plan is sold as a pack of profiles, for people running more than one brand. It adds those extra profiles, a domain you own, links that open a specific tab, custom previews when the page is shared, and beta features such as an AI chat. Linktree, Beacons, Stan Store, Later, and Shorby are the other tools people weigh it against.

It's a US product from 2020. A travel blog, a real-estate agent, an artist, a speaker, a bridal makeup artist, and a gaming creator are the kinds of customers in the reviews. One URL holds the work. The follower doesn't have to hunt across five profiles.
